title: Market Run, Week 4
dek: Ollie Gordon II is the only Miami back standing after Achane's ACL, and he is the first name on this week's list.
author: Chef Hazy
intro_md:
Week 3 broke three backfields. De'Von Achane is done for the year, Travis Etienne Jr. is out for Week 4 and longer, and Breece Hall is week to week. That puts the running backs at the top of the shop, with a rookie tight end right behind them.

FAAB ranges are percent of a 100 budget, written for 10 to 14 team leagues in full PPR. Rostered figures are from public waiver pages Tuesday morning; a blank means no clean number was available.
outro_md: The Menu lands Wednesday with every one of these players ranked. Claims first, lineups after.

adds.why: Gordon was the only active Miami back after Achane went down: 17 carries, 41 yards, a goal-line touchdown and 3 catches for 14 yards. Achane is on IR for the season, so this window runs as long as Gordon holds off Jaylen Wright.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 20 to 30 percent of FAAB. Top priority.

adds.why: Travis Etienne Jr. re-aggravated his hamstring after 13 carries for 54 yards, and the Saints already ruled him out for Monday against ATL. Kamara moves from a supporting role into the lead job, with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson behind him.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 15 to 25 percent of FAAB. Start him as a flex against ATL.

adds.why: Sadiq caught 7 of 8 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown at DET on a season-high 38 snaps with Mason Taylor out with a thumb injury. Before Sunday he sat at a 40 percent route share, so Taylor's return is the one thing that caps him.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 12 to 20 percent of FAAB. Start him @CHI if Taylor sits again.

adds.why: Allen played all 17 snaps after Breece Hall left at DET and has 19 carries for 61 yards on the year. Isaiah Davis has not taken an offensive snap, so Allen is the back while Hall is week to week.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 8 to 12 percent of FAAB. Flex him @CHI if Hall is out.

adds.why: Harris led the Chargers with 7 targets, 6 catches and 76 yards vs BUF, all career highs. He ran a route on 27 of 43 dropbacks, so the role is growing but still part time.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB. Bench him until the route share clears 75 percent.

adds.why: Allen caught 6 of 9 targets for 63 yards and a touchdown vs HOU with Alec Pierce out with a heel injury. That is 20 targets in three games, and it tilts toward him every week Pierce sits.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB. A PPR flex while Pierce is out.

adds.why: Wilson has drawn exactly 6 targets in each of Pittsburgh's three games and led the team Sunday with a 38-yard touchdown vs CIN. His snap share dipped to 39 percent, so he is earning looks on limited playing time.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 3 to 5 percent of FAAB. Bench stash until the snaps come back.

adds.why: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and 3 touchdowns at DET, spreading the scores to Garrett Wilson, Sadiq and Jeremy Ruckert. He also took 5 sacks, and Chicago's defense just held PHI to 7 points.
adds.verdict: Stream him @CHI, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, if your starter is Mayfield or on bye.

adds.why: Higbee caught 8 of 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown at DEN once Terrance Ferguson hurt his ankle, whose route share fell to 16 percent. Ferguson is unlikely for Week 4 and Colby Parkinson has an AC sprain.
adds.verdict: Stream him against PHI, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB, if Ferguson is ruled out.

stashes.why: Wright held the No. 2 job in camp and sat Week 3 with a stinger. Miami has not signed a back, so Wright and Gordon are the backfield once he is cleared.
stashes.verdict: Stash him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB. He splits with Gordon the week he is healthy.

stashes.why: Miller is in line for expanded work with Etienne out for an extended stretch, and Kamara has not carried a lead load yet this year.
stashes.verdict: Stash him in 12-team leagues and deeper, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB.

stashes.why: Davis has not taken an offensive snap in three games, but he is the only other back on the Jets roster with Hall hurt and he won camp buzz for the No. 2 job.
stashes.verdict: Stash him in 14-team leagues only, 0 to 1 percent. Bench him until he gets a carry.

drops.why: Torn ACL on his third carry vs KC. He is on IR for the season.
drops.verdict: Drop him unless your league has an open IR slot.

drops.why: One target for 8 yards vs NE on a day Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdowns. He has 13 targets to Parker Washington's 23 through three weeks and no touchdowns.
drops.verdict: Cut him for any of the top six adds above.

drops.why: Worthy led KC receivers with 43 snaps but ran only 19 routes and drew 2 targets. Most of his snaps come without a route.
drops.verdict: Cut him for Sadiq, Harris or Keenan Allen.

drops.why: Three carries for minus 4 yards at MIN and 2.1 yards per carry on the season. Bucky Irving out-snapped him 36 to 32, and an undrafted rookie is now at quarterback.
drops.verdict: Cut him for any running back on this list.

mnf.text: Chicago beat Philadelphia 27-7 with Case Keenum at quarterback. D'Andre Swift carried 20 times for 84 yards against his old team. Start Swift as your RB2 vs NYJ.

Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain with a three to four week timeline, and Tyson Bagent is the likely Week 4 starter. Leave Keenum and Bagent on waivers. Hold Rome Odunze; he dropped a wide-open touchdown, which is a better sign than no target at all.
Saquon Barkley ran 15 times for 82 yards, 73 of them in the first half, and Dallas Goedert sat with a knee injury. Start Barkley in Week 4, no change.
